How to read this record

each rule is read on axes: the comparison it reads with its interval, whether the rule as declared is met, when it was declared against its evidence, how many independent units it rests on, and anything wrong with what it rests on. No single word stands for all of that.

What the words on this page mean
open (question)
no call has closed it. A call on the question closes it: answered (accept), dropped (reject), parked, stopped, pivoted or shipped; investigate and continue keep it open. A finding or an interpretation does not make that call.
note (on a question)
recorded words on what meeting a rule would mean for the question. A note counts only while its rule is met; rb computes the finding and never asserts the inverse.
Computed comparison
rb's reading of a declared reversal between two rules: both numbers and intervals stay visible, and it makes no call on the question.
headline
rb's one line on a question's evidence, the first that applies: No rule tests this question yet (rules are filed here but none is linked to it), Evidence needs review (an integrity problem), No evidence recorded yet, Measured differences; uncertainty remains (an interval includes 0), Evidence includes point estimates only (a reading has no interval), else Evidence available for review.
rule written before the results
the rule was declared before the evidence it reads existed: a test planned in advance.
rule written after the results
the rule or its question link was declared after the evidence existed or after the data was seen: never read as a test planned in advance.
no interval
one estimate with no interval, so how much it could vary is unknown. rb gives one from 3 units, and none across fixed design cells.
Uncertainty remains
unresolved: the interval includes 0.
Fixed design cells
the reading spans fixed design choices: each cell is read on its own, with how many meet and their range, and no sampling interval across cells.
Reversal observed; repeatability uncertain
the two sides of a declared reversal measured opposite directions, but not both with intervals clear of 0.
rb's interval
95%, from 3 units: a Student t interval when the arms pair up by their unit, Welch (unpaired) when they never share one.
straddles
the interval crosses the rule's threshold: the rule word holds on the estimate, not across the whole interval.
rule
a threshold or comparison declared for a question; commands call it a criterion.
can't tell yet
there are results, but they don't settle the rule: it needs an interval, more units, or the metric's direction.
result
gain or loss (the interval clear of 0, read in the metric's direction), unresolved (the interval includes 0), equivalent (inside a declared margin), no interval (one estimate, no interval yet), measured (a level), higher or lower (the metric has no direction), not tested.
timing
declared before the evidence (before its runs, when only its baseline's runs came first: timing is read on the subject's runs); after the evidence existed; after the data was seen; order unknown.
units
the independent units a reading rests on. A repeat checks a run and adds no unit; a reanalysis adds none.
checks
problems with what a finding depends on (a stale source, an undeclared difference, a record edited outside rb). ok when there are none. Not the repository's own checks.
estimate meets the rule
met on the estimate, not across the whole interval; never drawn green.
verified
the named file, run or database row states this setting's value. It does not mean a run used it. provisional: given, not checked.
open (experiment)
planned: an experiment nothing tests yet. open: evidence and no call. accepted, rejected, investigating, parked, stopped, pivoted, shipped: what the latest call on it made it.
locked
the spec and rules are locked; a later change is recorded as an amendment.
not locked
rules and settings can still change; a freeze locks them.
not tested
no results for this rule yet: no recorded run reads this comparison
measured
one arm on its own, with its interval, so neither better nor worse
command (as given)
--command records what produced the numbers. rb did not run it.
not confirmed
it waits to be confirmed with rb in a terminal; until then it reads as a note, never as a call made or an answer.
reconstructible
present, changed, remote, reconstructible or lost: reconstructible means no copy is recorded, but how to get it again is.
gain
the interval is clear of 0 on the better side.
loss
the interval is clear of 0 on the worse side.
unresolved
the interval includes 0, which is not evidence of no difference.
equivalent
the interval lies inside the margin an equivalence rule declares.
reproduced
a rule from a cited source or from the record this one was cloned from, met by the runs recorded here.
not reproduced
a rule from a cited source or from the record this one was cloned from, not met by the runs recorded here.
paired difference
each unit's subject minus its reference, averaged over the units.
cited
a number someone else stated (a paper's table, say), checked against the source's own words.
margin
how far the value the rule judges (the estimate, an interval bound or the worst unit) sits from its threshold: positive inside it, negative outside. Not a declared equivalence or noninferiority margin.
question link
the question a rule's finding bears on, with the recorded words on what meeting the rule would mean for it.
identity
how exactly a resource is named: exact (the hash of its bytes), version (a release) or name only.
amended
changed after the rules and settings were locked; the change, its reason and what it changed from are kept.

How to read this record

each rule is read on axes: the comparison it reads with its interval, whether the rule as declared is met, when it was declared against its evidence, how many independent units it rests on, and anything wrong with what it rests on. No single word stands for all of that.

findings are computed, never stored, so regenerate this file after new runs. If this page and rb status ever disagree, rb status is right.

What the words on this page mean
open (question)
no call has closed it. A call on the question closes it: answered (accept), dropped (reject), parked, stopped, pivoted or shipped; investigate and continue keep it open. A finding or an interpretation does not make that call.
note (on a question)
recorded words on what meeting a rule would mean for the question. A note counts only while its rule is met; rb computes the finding and never asserts the inverse.
Computed comparison
rb's reading of a declared reversal between two rules: both numbers and intervals stay visible, and it makes no call on the question.
headline
rb's one line on a question's evidence, the first that applies: No rule tests this question yet (rules are filed here but none is linked to it), Evidence needs review (an integrity problem), No evidence recorded yet, Measured differences; uncertainty remains (an interval includes 0), Evidence includes point estimates only (a reading has no interval), else Evidence available for review.
rule written before the results
the rule was declared before the evidence it reads existed: a test planned in advance.
rule written after the results
the rule or its question link was declared after the evidence existed or after the data was seen: never read as a test planned in advance.
no interval
one estimate with no interval, so how much it could vary is unknown. rb gives one from 3 units, and none across fixed design cells.
Uncertainty remains
unresolved: the interval includes 0.
Fixed design cells
the reading spans fixed design choices: each cell is read on its own, with how many meet and their range, and no sampling interval across cells.
Reversal observed; repeatability uncertain
the two sides of a declared reversal measured opposite directions, but not both with intervals clear of 0.
rb's interval
95%, from 3 units: a Student t interval when the arms pair up by their unit, Welch (unpaired) when they never share one.
straddles
the interval crosses the rule's threshold: the rule word holds on the estimate, not across the whole interval.
rule
a threshold or comparison declared for a question; commands call it a criterion.
can't tell yet
there are results, but they don't settle the rule: it needs an interval, more units, or the metric's direction.
result
gain or loss (the interval clear of 0, read in the metric's direction), unresolved (the interval includes 0), equivalent (inside a declared margin), no interval (one estimate, no interval yet), measured (a level), higher or lower (the metric has no direction), not tested.
timing
declared before the evidence (before its runs, when only its baseline's runs came first: timing is read on the subject's runs); after the evidence existed; after the data was seen; order unknown.
units
the independent units a reading rests on. A repeat checks a run and adds no unit; a reanalysis adds none.
checks
problems with what a finding depends on (a stale source, an undeclared difference, a record edited outside rb). ok when there are none. Not the repository's own checks.
estimate meets the rule
met on the estimate, not across the whole interval; never drawn green.
verified
the named file, run or database row states this setting's value. It does not mean a run used it. provisional: given, not checked.
open (experiment)
planned: an experiment nothing tests yet. open: evidence and no call. accepted, rejected, investigating, parked, stopped, pivoted, shipped: what the latest call on it made it.
locked
the spec and rules are locked; a later change is recorded as an amendment.
not locked
rules and settings can still change; a freeze locks them.
not tested
no results for this rule yet: no recorded run reads this comparison
measured
one arm on its own, with its interval, so neither better nor worse
command (as given)
--command records what produced the numbers. rb did not run it.
not confirmed
it waits to be confirmed with rb in a terminal; until then it reads as a note, never as a call made or an answer.
reconstructible
present, changed, remote, reconstructible or lost: reconstructible means no copy is recorded, but how to get it again is.
gain
the interval is clear of 0 on the better side.
loss
the interval is clear of 0 on the worse side.
unresolved
the interval includes 0, which is not evidence of no difference.
equivalent
the interval lies inside the margin an equivalence rule declares.
reproduced
a rule from a cited source or from the record this one was cloned from, met by the runs recorded here.
not reproduced
a rule from a cited source or from the record this one was cloned from, not met by the runs recorded here.
paired difference
each unit's subject minus its reference, averaged over the units.
cited
a number someone else stated (a paper's table, say), checked against the source's own words.
margin
how far the value the rule judges (the estimate, an interval bound or the worst unit) sits from its threshold: positive inside it, negative outside. Not a declared equivalence or noninferiority margin.
question link
the question a rule's finding bears on, with the recorded words on what meeting the rule would mean for it.
identity
how exactly a resource is named: exact (the hash of its bytes), version (a release) or name only.

How to read this record

each rule is read on axes: the comparison it reads with its interval, whether the rule as declared is met, when it was declared against its evidence, how many independent units it rests on, and anything wrong with what it rests on. No single word stands for all of that.

What the words on this page mean
open (question)
no call has closed it. A call on the question closes it: answered (accept), dropped (reject), parked, stopped, pivoted or shipped; investigate and continue keep it open. A finding or an interpretation does not make that call.
note (on a question)
recorded words on what meeting a rule would mean for the question. A note counts only while its rule is met; rb computes the finding and never asserts the inverse.
Computed comparison
rb's reading of a declared reversal between two rules: both numbers and intervals stay visible, and it makes no call on the question.
headline
rb's one line on a question's evidence, the first that applies: No rule tests this question yet (rules are filed here but none is linked to it), Evidence needs review (an integrity problem), No evidence recorded yet, Measured differences; uncertainty remains (an interval includes 0), Evidence includes point estimates only (a reading has no interval), else Evidence available for review.
rule written before the results
the rule was declared before the evidence it reads existed: a test planned in advance.
rule written after the results
the rule or its question link was declared after the evidence existed or after the data was seen: never read as a test planned in advance.
no interval
one estimate with no interval, so how much it could vary is unknown. rb gives one from 3 units, and none across fixed design cells.
Uncertainty remains
unresolved: the interval includes 0.
Fixed design cells
the reading spans fixed design choices: each cell is read on its own, with how many meet and their range, and no sampling interval across cells.
Reversal observed; repeatability uncertain
the two sides of a declared reversal measured opposite directions, but not both with intervals clear of 0.
rb's interval
95%, from 3 units: a Student t interval when the arms pair up by their unit, Welch (unpaired) when they never share one.
straddles
the interval crosses the rule's threshold: the rule word holds on the estimate, not across the whole interval.
rule
a threshold or comparison declared for a question; commands call it a criterion.
can't tell yet
there are results, but they don't settle the rule: it needs an interval, more units, or the metric's direction.
result
gain or loss (the interval clear of 0, read in the metric's direction), unresolved (the interval includes 0), equivalent (inside a declared margin), no interval (one estimate, no interval yet), measured (a level), higher or lower (the metric has no direction), not tested.
timing
declared before the evidence (before its runs, when only its baseline's runs came first: timing is read on the subject's runs); after the evidence existed; after the data was seen; order unknown.
units
the independent units a reading rests on. A repeat checks a run and adds no unit; a reanalysis adds none.
checks
problems with what a finding depends on (a stale source, an undeclared difference, a record edited outside rb). ok when there are none. Not the repository's own checks.
estimate meets the rule
met on the estimate, not across the whole interval; never drawn green.
verified
the named file, run or database row states this setting's value. It does not mean a run used it. provisional: given, not checked.
open (experiment)
planned: an experiment nothing tests yet. open: evidence and no call. accepted, rejected, investigating, parked, stopped, pivoted, shipped: what the latest call on it made it.
locked
the spec and rules are locked; a later change is recorded as an amendment.
not locked
rules and settings can still change; a freeze locks them.
not tested
no results for this rule yet: no recorded run reads this comparison
measured
one arm on its own, with its interval, so neither better nor worse
command (as given)
--command records what produced the numbers. rb did not run it.
not confirmed
it waits to be confirmed with rb in a terminal; until then it reads as a note, never as a call made or an answer.
reconstructible
present, changed, remote, reconstructible or lost: reconstructible means no copy is recorded, but how to get it again is.
gain
the interval is clear of 0 on the better side.
loss
the interval is clear of 0 on the worse side.
unresolved
the interval includes 0, which is not evidence of no difference.
equivalent
the interval lies inside the margin an equivalence rule declares.
reproduced
a rule from a cited source or from the record this one was cloned from, met by the runs recorded here.
not reproduced
a rule from a cited source or from the record this one was cloned from, not met by the runs recorded here.
paired difference
each unit's subject minus its reference, averaged over the units.
cited
a number someone else stated (a paper's table, say), checked against the source's own words.
margin
how far the value the rule judges (the estimate, an interval bound or the worst unit) sits from its threshold: positive inside it, negative outside. Not a declared equivalence or noninferiority margin.
question link
the question a rule's finding bears on, with the recorded words on what meeting the rule would mean for it.
identity
how exactly a resource is named: exact (the hash of its bytes), version (a release) or name only.
amended
changed after the rules and settings were locked; the change, its reason and what it changed from are kept.
